name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries attempt to obtain account credentials (hashes or clear-text passwords) from the operating system and software so they can log on to other systems.
detection: Monitor access to credential stores such as LSASS, the SAM and NTDS.dit, and EDR credential-theft alerts.
mitigation: Credential Guard, LSA protection, privileged access management and limiting credential exposure on endpoints.

name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
description: Adversaries read the memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe) to recover password hashes, Kerberos tickets and sometimes clear-text credentials. Common tooling includes Mimikatz, ProcDump and the comsvcs.dll MiniDump export.
detection: Monitor process access to lsass.exe (Sysmon Event ID 10) with suspicious GrantedAccess masks, creation of .dmp files, and command lines referencing sekurlsa or MiniDump.
mitigation: Enable Credential Guard and LSA protection (RunAsPPL), restrict debug privileges, use Privileged Access Workstations and limit credential overlap between tiers.

name: OS Credential Dumping: DCSync
description: Adversaries abuse directory replication APIs to impersonate a domain controller and request password data (including the KRBTGT hash) for any account.
detection: Monitor Windows Event 4662 for replication extended rights (DS-Replication-Get-Changes and -All) requested by accounts that are not domain controllers.
mitigation: Audit and minimise accounts with replication rights, monitor privileged groups, and rotate the KRBTGT password twice if compromise is suspected.

name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
description: Adversaries request Kerberos service tickets for accounts with SPNs and crack the RC4-encrypted ticket offline to recover the service account password.
detection: Look for bursts of Event 4769 with ticket encryption type 0x17 (RC4) from a single user, particularly for many distinct services.
mitigation: Use long random passwords or group Managed Service Accounts for service accounts, enforce AES encryption and limit SPN-bearing privileged accounts.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries guess passwords systematically to gain access to accounts when credentials are unknown.
detection: Track failed authentication counts per account and per source (Event 4625, sshd failures) and alert on thresholds or success following failures.
mitigation: Enforce multi-factor authentication, account lockout policies and strong password policies; block abusive sources.

name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
description: Adversaries try a small number of common passwords against many accounts to avoid lockouts.
detection: Detect a single source failing authentication for many distinct accounts in a short window.
mitigation: Multi-factor authentication, banned-password lists and conditional access policies.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell to execute commands, download payloads and run code in memory, often using encoded commands, download cradles and execution-policy bypass flags.
detection: Enable Script Block Logging (Event 4104) and process command-line auditing; alert on -EncodedCommand, DownloadString, FromBase64String and hidden windows.
mitigation: Constrained Language Mode, application control (WDAC/AppLocker), AMSI integration and removing PowerShell v2.

name: System Services: Service Execution
description: Adversaries create or abuse Windows services to execute commands, frequently remotely via tools such as PsExec.
detection: Monitor service installation events (7045/4697) with unusual binary paths and PSEXESVC artifacts.
mitigation: Restrict administrative rights, block remote service creation from non-admin hosts and monitor admin share usage.

name: User Execution: Malicious File
description: A user is tricked into opening a malicious file that executes adversary code.
detection: Endpoint protection detections, Office applications spawning interpreters, and execution from user download directories.
mitigation: User training, attachment sandboxing, application control and blocking macros from the internet.

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
description: Adversaries register scheduled tasks to execute malicious code at logon, at boot or on a timer, providing persistence and sometimes privilege escalation.
detection: Monitor Event 4698 and schtasks.exe /create command lines, focusing on tasks that run scripts from user-writable paths.
mitigation: Restrict task creation permissions and audit scheduled tasks across the estate.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys
description: Adversaries add programs to Run or RunOnce registry keys so they launch at user logon.
detection: Monitor registry writes to CurrentVersion\Run keys (Sysmon Event 13) and compare against a known-good baseline.
mitigation: Application control and restricting registry permissions.

name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
description: Adversaries create or modify services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads with SYSTEM privileges.
detection: Monitor new service installation events and service binary paths outside standard directories.
mitigation: Limit privileges for service creation and audit service configuration changes.

name: Create Account
description: Adversaries create local, domain or cloud accounts to maintain access.
detection: Monitor account creation events (4720) and correlate with change-management records.
mitigation: Multi-factor authentication for privileged operations and least-privilege account management.

name: Account Manipulation
description: Adversaries modify accounts or group memberships, for example adding an account to Domain Admins, to maintain or elevate access.
detection: Monitor group membership changes (4728/4732/4756) for privileged groups.
mitigation: Privileged account management, just-in-time administration and alerting on privileged group changes.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
description: Adversaries abuse sudo configuration or cached sudo credentials on Linux and macOS to execute commands as root.
detection: Audit sudo logs for unusual commands such as shell spawns, shadow file access or user creation.
mitigation: Tighten sudoers rules, require password re-entry (timestamp_timeout=0) and restrict file permissions.

name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
description: Adversaries clear Windows event logs to hide their activity.
detection: Event 1102 (Security log cleared) and 104 (System log cleared), and wevtutil cl command lines. Forward logs off-host so clearing is still visible.
mitigation: Centralised log collection, restricting permissions to clear logs and protecting audit configuration.

name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
description: Adversaries disable or reconfigure security tools such as antivirus or EDR to avoid detection.
detection: Monitor changes to Defender preferences (Set-MpPreference), stopped security services and tamper-protection alerts.
mitigation: Enable tamper protection, restrict local administrator rights and monitor security tool health centrally.

name: Account Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate local and domain accounts and groups to plan privilege escalation and lateral movement.
detection: Monitor net user/group, nltest, whoami /all and AD enumeration tools such as BloodHound/SharpHound, especially from non-admin users.
mitigation: Limit what standard users can enumerate and monitor LDAP query volume.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries scan networks to identify listening services that can be exploited or used for lateral movement.
detection: Detect a host connecting to many ports or hosts in a short window and execution of scanning tools.
mitigation: Network segmentation, host firewalls and intrusion prevention.

name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Adversaries use valid accounts to log on to systems over RDP.
detection: Monitor logon type 10 events, especially from unusual sources or for accounts that do not normally use RDP.
mitigation: Restrict RDP to jump hosts, require MFA and Network Level Authentication, and limit Remote Desktop Users group membership.

name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Adversaries use administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$) with valid credentials to copy tools and execute code on remote hosts.
detection: Monitor Event 5140/5145 for admin share access from workstations and file writes to ADMIN$.
mitigation: Disable admin shares where not needed, use LAPS for local admin passwords and block SMB between workstations.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
description: Adversaries use WMI locally or remotely to execute commands and gather information.
detection: Monitor wmic /node: and Invoke-WmiMethod usage and WmiPrvSE.exe spawning shells.
mitigation: Restrict remote WMI/WinRM to administrative hosts and apply attack surface reduction rules.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
description: Adversaries communicate with command-and-control servers over HTTP/HTTPS to blend in with normal traffic, often with periodic beaconing.
detection: Look for periodic connections with consistent intervals and sizes, rare destinations and unusual user agents.
mitigation: Egress filtering through proxies, TLS inspection where permitted and network intrusion prevention.

name: Non-Standard Port
description: Adversaries use ports not typically associated with a protocol, such as 4444 or 8443, for command and control.
detection: Alert on outbound connections to uncommon ports from workstations and servers.
mitigation: Default-deny egress firewall rules and network intrusion prevention.

name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
description: Adversaries tunnel command-and-control traffic through DNS queries, often using long, high-entropy subdomains.
detection: Detect long or high-entropy query names, high query volume to one domain and newly registered or suspicious TLDs.
mitigation: Use protective DNS resolvers, block direct outbound DNS and sinkhole known malicious domains.

name: Remote Access Software
description: Adversaries install legitimate remote administration tools (AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, etc.) to maintain interactive access.
detection: Inventory and alert on execution of unsanctioned remote access software.
mitigation: Application control allow-lists and blocking remote access tool domains at the proxy.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
description: Adversaries steal data using protocols other than their command-and-control channel, such as FTP, SMTP or DNS.
detection: Monitor for unusually large outbound transfers and connections to destinations with no business history.
mitigation: Data loss prevention, egress filtering and network segmentation of sensitive data stores.

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
description: Adversaries upload stolen data to cloud storage services using tools such as rclone or MEGA clients.
detection: Detect rclone and similar tools, and large uploads to cloud storage domains not used by the business.
mitigation: Restrict web-based content and cloud storage destinations; deploy DLP controls.

name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
description: Adversaries compress and optionally encrypt collected data with tools such as 7-Zip or WinRAR before exfiltration.
detection: Monitor archiving utilities run against file shares or sensitive directories.
mitigation: Application control for archiving utilities on servers and DLP inspection.

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Adversaries delete Volume Shadow Copies, backup catalogues and recovery settings to prevent recovery, a strong precursor of ransomware encryption.
detection: Alert on vssadmin delete shadows, wmic shadowcopy delete, bcdedit recoveryenabled no and wbadmin delete.
mitigation: Offline/immutable backups, restricting access to backup infrastructure and blocking these utilities for non-admins.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Adversaries encrypt data on systems and network shares to disrupt availability and extort the victim (ransomware).
detection: Detect mass file renames or writes with new extensions, ransom note creation and high file-write entropy.
mitigation: Immutable offline backups, network segmentation, controlled folder access and rapid host isolation.

name: Network Denial of Service
description: Adversaries flood network resources to degrade or block availability of services.
detection: Monitor traffic volume baselines and upstream provider alerts.
mitigation: Upstream DDoS mitigation services, rate limiting and capacity planning.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries exploit weaknesses in internet-facing applications (SQL injection, deserialisation, JNDI injection, path traversal) to gain initial access.
detection: WAF and web server logs for injection patterns, unexpected child processes of web servers and new files in web roots.
mitigation: Prompt patching of internet-facing systems, web application firewalls, vulnerability scanning and application isolation.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Adversaries send emails with malicious attachments that execute code when opened.
detection: Email gateway detections, Office applications spawning shells and attachments executed from temp directories.
mitigation: Attachment sandboxing, macro blocking, user training and attack surface reduction rules.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to gain access, often bypassing controls and blending in.
detection: Logons from new locations or devices, logons without MFA, impossible travel and access outside normal hours.
mitigation: Multi-factor authentication, conditional access, privileged account management and credential hygiene.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries use valid accounts to log on to remote services (RDP, SMB, WinRM, SSH) and move between systems.
detection: Correlate remote logons and remote execution with account baselines and expected admin sources.
mitigation: Restrict remote services to jump hosts, enforce MFA and segment workstation-to-server traffic.
